name: Miller & Zois, Attorneys at Law
about: Miller & Zois, Attorneys at Law is a personal injury firm with a single office in Baltimore.

The firm states that it works on a contingency fee, with nothing to pay unless the case is won; the first consultation is free; its intake line is open around the clock; it will visit clients in hospital or at home.

google.source: Google Business Profile via Places API. 1 listing, counts summed and rating weighted by count

completeness.note: Categories, opening hours, photo count and description come from the Places API. The services list, the Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the API does not expose at any price, so they are not scored either way.

ahrefs.source: Ahrefs Site Explorer, batch endpoint, subdomains mode, organic figures for the United States

G1.evidence: Maryland does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

G2.evidence: 1 of the firm's attorneys share a surname with a disciplined attorney, and for Ronald V. Miller Jr. 2 of 9 decision(s) naming this surname have no searchable text, so they can be neither tied to nor ruled out against this attorney. The decisions that cannot be read are scans without searchable text, so this is a limit of the published record. Nothing here says the firm's attorney is that person.

G3.evidence: 1 physical location verified on Google Business Profile. Maryland publishes no business register we can query. SDAT's entity search is a form rather than a dataset, its bulk data is sold rather than published, and the state's open data portal carries a count of businesses instead of the register. This is a limit of the published record and not something the firm can change.

G5.evidence: Site has served over HTTPS, a working phone number published, 3 named attorneys published.
G5.source: Public crawl of the firm's own site

G6.evidence: 118 public client reviews across 1 Google listing, above the 10 minimum, and the firm's domain has been registered since 2002-09-06, so it has been operating for more than a year
G6.source: Google Places API and the domain's registration date over RDAP

fee_statement: All of our motorcycle accident cases are on a contingency fee basis.

accountability.evidence: no bar or trial lawyers' association named on the pages we read · no professional liability cover disclosed, which is not scored here: plaintiff firms in this market do not publish it, and an absence shared by every firm separates none of them

score.verdict: 2 of 5 eligibility gates passed. 3 could not be answered from the available records (G1, G2, G3) and do not count against the firm. Strongest pillar: C; most headroom in pillar A (0/25).

subs.label: Experience
subs.evidence: Maryland publishes no attorney register we can query, so years since admission cannot be established here for any firm and this is not scored.

subs.label: Roster verifiability
subs.evidence: Maryland publishes no attorney register we can query, so the roster is not verified here and this is not scored.

subs.label: Accountability
subs.evidence: no bar or trial lawyers' association named on the pages we read · no professional liability cover disclosed, which is not scored here: plaintiff firms in this market do not publish it, and an absence shared by every firm separates none of them

subs.label: Results published
subs.evidence: 15 results published on the firm's own site, counted from stated amounts

subs.label: Specificity
subs.evidence: 5 case types named; no court or county named, so no result can be looked up

subs.label: Results disclosure
subs.evidence: No prior-results disclaimer on the results page, which the New York advertising rules effectively require

subs.label: Authentic volume
subs.evidence: 119 Google reviews · Google Business Profile via Places API. 1 listing, counts summed and rating weighted by count

subs.label: Rating quality
subs.evidence: Google rating 4.2 over 119 reviews → Bayesian 4.49 (prior 4.83 weighted as 100 reviews, from 527 scored firms) · single platform, Google only

subs.label: Review recency
subs.evidence: 3 of 5 sampled reviews are from the last 12 months (newest 2026-03-30) · a sample of five per business listing, not every review

subs.label: Complaint share
subs.evidence: 0 of 5 sampled reviews rate 1 or 2 stars · a sample, so this is the shape of the complaints rather than a count of them

subs.label: Website trust & experience
subs.evidence: CWV fail · no bar numbers on bios · no fee statement · privacy policy · disclaimer · fresh content

subs.label: Search authority
subs.evidence: DR 56 → 96th pct of 26-firm cohort (median 19) 3/3 · 3,287 referring domains, 100th pct 2/2 · 8,279 organic keywords / 36,489 visits·mo, 100th pct 2/2 · brand demand 0/1 (pending)

subs.label: Local presence
subs.evidence: 1 operational Google Business Profile listing · 10 or more photos, which is where the API stops counting · 5 categories, hours published, which almost every listing here has and so separates nobody · the services list, Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the Places API does not expose, and NAP consistency across citations and local-pack rank have no source here, so the rest of this sub-factor leaves the scale rather than being scored as unearned

subs.label: Content, E-E-A-T & schema
subs.evidence: JSON-LD detected 1/1 · not assessed on any firm yet, so content depth and earned media and AI citations leave the scale (4 pts)

subs.label: Free consult & fee transparency
subs.evidence: Free consultation · “All of our motorcycle accident cases are on a contingency fee basis.” · the fee percentage itself is not published

operating.source: Domain registration date over RDAP, which is a lower bound on how long the firm has been operating rather than its founding date

logo.source: The icon the firm's own site declares, copied here rather than hot-linked

court_dockets.note: A docket search found 15 case(s) naming this firm alongside sanction or consumer-protection language, none of which is a finding against it: a firm appears in such a docket by arguing about sanctions, or by bringing consumer-protection claims for its clients. Text search over this collection cannot separate an action against a firm from its ordinary practice, so nothing here is settled by it.
court_dockets.source: CourtListener docket search (Free Law Project), RECAP collection, screening only
